items.title: TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback is red on Go 1.27: its probe reuses a kept-alive connection after the WSL listener closes
items.body:
`TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback` (`internal/gateway/wsl_test.go`) fails 3 of 3 on main c158b0439 with go1.27.2 darwin/arm64, and passes 3 of 3 there with go1.26.8 (go.mod's, CI's). I couldn't find it filed. #3547 and #3549 are the other Go 1.27 reds from the same run.

```
--- FAIL: TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback (10.03s)
    wsl_test.go:165: WSL network gone: http://[::1]:58208/ answers = true
```

Run, in a sandbox HOME at c158b0439 with nothing else changed:

```sh
GOTOOLCHAIN=local   go test -tags nogui -count=3 -run '^TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback$' ./internal/gateway/   # go1.27.2: FAIL
GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8 go test -tags nogui -count=3 -run '^TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback$' ./internal/gateway/   # ok
```

**Likely cause, checked once:** `answers()` makes a new `http.Client` with no Transport, so every probe goes through `http.DefaultTransport` and its pool of kept-alive connections. After "WSL network up", the pool holds a connection to `[::1]:port`. Closing the WSL listener doesn't close connections it has already accepted, so the "WSL network gone" probe is answered over that connection, and on Go 1.27 it holds for the whole 10s wait. With only the probe changed to `&http.Client{Timeout: time.Second, Transport: &http.Transport{DisableKeepAlives: true}}`, the test passes 3 of 3 on go1.27.2. Not checked: what changed between 1.26 and 1.27 to make the old connection last the wait.

items.title: [bug] sessions: a Claude Code fork subagent's copy of its parent's reply is counted twice (branch ready; PRs are collaborators-only)
items.body:
Branch: [fish2lab/magpie `sessions-claude-fork-copy`](https://github.com/fish2lab/magpie/tree/sessions-claude-fork-copy), one commit, [df11f97](https://github.com/fish2lab/magpie/commit/df11f97d0e16279d889b0f0da8a353b6d903661d), on origin/main 7d075df. I'm filing it as an issue because PRs here are limited to collaborators.

```
git fetch https://github.com/fish2lab/magpie sessions-claude-fork-copy && git cherry-pick df11f97
```

## What's wrong

A Claude Code fork subagent's transcript (`<session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`, here from Claude Code 2.1.302) opens with a `fork-context-ref` line. Next comes a copy of the parent's reply that started the fork, with the same `message.id` and `requestId`, now marked `isSidechain: true` with the fork's `agentId`. Then comes the fork's own prompt. The parent's main file already counts that reply, and the sessions reader dedupes calls only within a file. So `magpie sessions` and the stats count the reply once more for every fork.

## The fix

Subsystem: sessions (`internal/sessions`, the Claude Code reader). No subsystem reference documents how Claude transcripts are counted, so no page changes.

- Trigger: a `fork-context-ref` line. The reader sets `state.ForkHead` and skips assistant lines until the file's first user line. It does this both in the fast path (`claudeLine`) and in the full parse (`claudeFull`). The first user line clears the flag, and everything after it is counted as before.
- Before: the copied reply counted once in the parent's file and again in each fork's file. After: it counts once, in the parent's file.
- State: `ForkHead` is kept in the parse cache (`fork_head`), so a read that resumes inside the head still skips. `cacheVersion` goes from 22 to 23, so files parsed before are read again.
- Files without a `fork-context-ref` line read as before. These include ordinary subagents, workflow agents and main transcripts.

## Verification

Run at df11f97 (on origin/main 7d075df), go1.27.3 darwin/arm64:

- `gofmt -l` is clean.
- Vet is clean: `go vet ./...`, `GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui ./...` and `GOOS=windows go vet ./...`.
- Builds are ok: `go build`, `GOOS=linux go build -tags nogui` and `GOOS=windows go build`.
- `go test -tags nogui -count=1 ./...` in a sandbox HOME with Go's caches pinned: 69 packages ok, including `internal/sessions` (ok, 73s). A few packages are red, and they are red in the same way on origin/main 7d075df without this change:
  - `internal/provider`: #3632 (ok in 71s with `TestUnreadLoginsWriteErrorsKeepCredentials` skipped)
  - `internal/gateway`: `TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON` and `FuzzMarshalRaw` (#3547), `TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget` (#3549), `TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback` (#3680)
  - `internal/plugin`: `TestPluginSOCKSProxy` (#2207)
- Broken by hand: I put the old `claude.go` and `sessions.go` back and kept the new test. `TestClaudeForkSubagentCountsParentReplyOnce` then fails with `session: {Input:250 Output:25 CacheRead:30 ...}, want {Input:150 Output:15 CacheRead:20 ...}`. With the change restored, it passes.

I also checked against real data. I copied one real session (its main file and its one fork) into a sandbox, with HOME, the XDG dirs and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` all pointing there, and ran `magpie sessions --json` with binaries built from origin/main and from this branch:

| | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| input | 238 | 236 |
| output | 153,562 | 150,944 |
| cache read | 24,171,440 | 24,041,229 |
| cache write | 388,781 | 387,933 |

The branch's numbers equal that session's calls deduped by `message.id` + `requestId` across all of its files, as counted by an independent reader, [git-tab](https://github.com/fish2lab/git-tab)'s Claude Code adapter.

Not tried:

- Cowork transcripts, which use the same reader.
- Running on Linux or Windows; only the GOOS vet and builds above were run. The change has no platform code.

## Found while checking, not changed here

I compared 115 sessions from the last 30 days against git-tab, and 100 matched to the cent. Three other differences come from magpie behavior I left alone. I can open a separate issue for any of them if useful:

- `sessions` and the stats price each model's total at its base tier (`p.At(0)` in `sessions.go` and `stats.go`). So Claude Haiku 5.5's rate for prompts above 100K tokens ($0.50/$2.50 per MTok, against $0.10/$0.50) is never applied. One pi session on Haiku 5.5 had identical tokens on both sides. It cost $0.12 in magpie, against $0.52 when each request is priced at its tier.
- DeepSeek's peak-hour price is not applied. It is 2× on weekdays 9:00–12:00 and 14:00–18:00 Beijing time ([pricing page](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/quick_start/pricing)). Two pi sessions on deepseek-flash that ran entirely in peak hours came out at half their price.
- A forked or resumed Claude Code session copies its parent's history into a new main file under a new `sessionId`. Per-session totals then count the copied calls in both sessions. In one fork the copies made up 95% of its listed cost: $6.62 listed, against $0.31 for its own calls.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

items.title: [feat] Settings › Observability: Test the OTLP connection (branch ready; PRs are collaborators-only)
items.body:
## The problem In Settings › Observability, once the OTLP endpoint and headers are filled in, nothing says whether they work. A wrong key, a host without `/api/public/otel`, or `http://` where the collector redirects to `https://` all end the same way: `otel: traces export failed; batch dropped` in the log, and nothing in the collector. The only check is to send real traffic and go look in Langfuse. An SSH or database client has a Test connection button for this; Observability has none. ## What the branch does **Test connection**, a row under OTLP headers on the Collector connection card, with a Test button. It sends an **empty export** (`{"resourceSpans":[]}`, and `{"resourceMetrics":[]}` when Export metrics is on), so the collector checks the endpoint and headers and records nothing. The lines under the row say what it met: | Answer | What the row says | | --- | --- | | 2xx | Works: `` took a test export in N ms | | 401 / 403 | `` refused the headers (401): check the keys, and that they are for this host, then *The collector says: …* | | 404 / 405, or a web page answering | No collector answers at `` (404): check the endpoint's path. Langfuse's ends in /api/public/otel | | 3xx | `` redirects to `
`, and exports don't follow redirects: use that address as the endpoint | | other status | `` answered 503, then the collector's own message | | no connection | Couldn't reach ``: dial tcp: lookup …: no such host | | no answer in 3s | `` didn't answer within 3 seconds, so an export there would be dropped | Every string is in zh, zh-TW, ja and de. ## How it works, and why it says what an export would meet - `otlp.Check` sends the empty export **by the exporter's own code**. `otelClient` (the proxy in force, 3s, no redirect followed), `signalURL` and `exportRequest` were pulled out of `send` and are shared with it; `send`'s behaviour is unchanged, and the existing exporter tests pass as they were. - `POST /api/otel/test` tries `settings.OTelExport()`: the saved settings under any `MAGPIE_OTEL_*`, which is what the exporter sends to, with export **on or off** (so it can be tried before turning export on). It **takes no endpoint or headers from the request**, so the route can't be used to send the saved credentials anywhere else. The page waits for a field's pending save (`prefsQueue`) before it asks, so a value typed and not yet saved is the one tested. - Header values (whole, each long word, and Basic's decoded user and password) are taken out of anything the collector says back. HTML answers are never shown. - An unreadable `settings.json` is said as such, not as "no endpoint" (`settings.LoadChecked` first). - No new destination: the request goes only to the collector the user configured, with the headers they configured for it. ## Checked against the real Langfuse Cloud (US) The built binary (`magpie web`, `-tags nogui`) in a sandbox HOME, with its own gateway port, `MAGPIE_NO_ACCOUNTS=1` and `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, never the running magpie: | Saved settings | `POST /api/otel/test` answered | | --- | --- | | correct keys, export Off | `200`, "Works" in ~260 ms | | wrong secret key | `401` auth, "Invalid credentials. Confirm that you've configured the correct host." | | host without `/api/public/otel` | `404` path (Langfuse's HTML 404 page, not shown) | | `http://` instead of `https://` | `301` redirect, suggests `https://us.cloud.langfuse.com:443/api/public/otel`; saving that address → `200` | | Export metrics on | traces `200`, metrics `200` | | a host that doesn't resolve | network, "dial tcp: lookup …: no such host" | | nothing saved | 400 "Set the OTLP endpoint first" | - **The collector records nothing:** after three Tests, Langfuse's `GET /api/public/v2/observations` for that window returned 0 observations, while the same query over the hours before returns the project's real gateway traces. - **The secret never comes back:** neither the secret key nor its base64 appears in any answer. - **The real page:** driven in Chromium against the sandbox, with a wrong header typed (not saved) and Test clicked: the field was saved first, then tested, and the 401 and Langfuse's message showed. Screenshots below. ## The branch - Diff against main: https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/main...0xJchen:magpie:otel-test-connection - One commit, rebased on main `7499ebb5`: https://github.com/0xJchen/magpie/commit/7d9f65d30672 ```sh git fetch https://github.com/0xJchen/magpie.git otel-test-connection git cherry-pick 7d9f65d30672 ``` 14 files, +933 −15: `internal/otlp/check.go` (new), `internal/otlp/otel.go` (helpers shared with `send`), `internal/gui/oteltest.go` (new route), `internal/gui/api.go` (registration), `app.js` / `app.css` / `i18n.js` (the row), tests, `docs/reference.md` (OTLP export) and `docs/subsystems/plugin-runtime.md` (`plugins/otel`). **app.js size:** the row adds 2,769 bytes to app.js, and `TestCoreScriptBudget`'s two budgets are raised by exactly that, with the reason in their comments, as for other Settings rows. If you'd rather Observability's section moved into `plugins/otel`'s own client files first, I can do that as a separate commit. ## What was run (at 7d9f65d30, on main 7499ebb5) Go under a sandbox HOME, on go1.26.8 (go.mod's and CI's): - `gofmt -l` on the changed files prints nothing. `go vet ./...` for darwin, `GOOS=linux -tags nogui` and `GOOS=windows`, plus the three builds: ok. - **New tests:** `TestCheck*` (5, `-race`) and `TestOTelTest*` (3) pass. `otel-check.test.cjs` passes 12 of 12 in Chromium and in WebKit, in every language, at 1100 and 420 px wide. - **Each guarantee broken by hand,** with its test red, then restored: - headers dropped; - redirects followed; - proxy ignored; - a URL built apart from `signalURL`; - metrics skipped; - a 2xx web page taken as working; - header values not scrubbed; - a timeout read as a network fault; - `LoadChecked` dropped; - the request's endpoint taken; - `MAGPIE_OTEL_*` ignored; - the page not waiting for a pending save; - an answer kept after the endpoint changes; - the collector's words dropped; - the page as it is on main. - **`go test -tags nogui -timeout 45m ./...`:** 70 packages ok. The one red is `internal/provider`, #3632, which is red the same on main's own CI. On go1.27.2, four `internal/gateway` tests are red on main too and green on 1.26.8: #3547 (two tests), #3549, and `TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback`, which is unfiled. - **The whole GUI suite** (896 files, both engines, at c0985122 + this change; 7499ebb5 touches no GUI file): 27 files had a red. Each was run on main beside this branch under the same load, and none is red here and green on main. Filed: #3497, #2572, #3479, #3403, #3402, #3079, #3410, #3411, #3637, #3408, #3096, #3412, #3409, #3413, #3414, #2549, #2399, #3415, #1876. Unfiled but red on main: `quota-refresh-order` (since 09c0a844), `search-first`, `skill-gone`. Five were red under load only. - **Since then:** main moved to 19253f67 (the Routing plugin's own script). The commit applies onto it without conflict. The full record is in the commit body. ## Not tried - **Other collectors:** an OpenTelemetry Collector, Grafana Cloud, Honeycomb and self-hosted Langfuse weren't tried, only Langfuse Cloud (US). A collector that accepts an export without checking headers passes the Test. A 200 means the collector took the export, not that it keeps that signal: Langfuse answers 200 on `/v1/metrics` too, while the Export metrics row says to leave metrics off for it. - **Linux and Windows:** only vetted and built (`GOOS=linux`, `GOOS=windows`), not run. The change is an HTTP request and a Settings row, with nothing per-OS. - **The desktop window:** the page was tested in Playwright's Chromium and WebKit and in `magpie web`, not in the macOS app's own WebKit window.
